about.subtitle: Learn about the background, origins and open source information of GUGU WebUI.
about.source_desc: GUGU WebUI was originally inspired by the idea that the GUGUbot plugin should have its own WebUI. At that time GUGUbot was still relatively simple, so a dedicated WebUI was not added, but this sparked the idea of building a more general‑purpose WebUI plugin, which eventually became GUGU WebUI, originating from GUGUbot.

projects.gugubot_desc: The original automation bot and chat features that created the need for web management.
projects.cq_desc: Provides QQ‑side message forwarding and integration, extending how the server connects to the outside world.
projects.web_desc: An evolution based on the previous two, focusing on a more modern WebUI management experience.

about.opensource_desc: As an open source project, GUGU WebUI welcomes bug reports, pull requests, documentation updates and localization contributions.
about.thanks_desc: Thanks to all developers and server admins who contributed code, suggestions and testing to GUGU WebUI. Your support keeps this project evolving.

items.mcdr_repo_desc: Provides a rich MCDR plugin ecosystem, forming the foundation of this project’s features.
items.mc_server_info: Base implementation for querying Minecraft server status and player information.
items.mcdreforged_desc: MCDR core; the runtime platform this plugin depends on.
items.wolfgangfahl_desc: Implementation approach for threaded uvicorn was referenced.
items.minecraft_wiki_desc: Format specification for the RText parser.
items.mcstatus_desc: Python library for querying Minecraft Java Edition server status.

items.looseprince_desc: Feature design, documentation, web design and frontend implementation.
items.xuek66_desc: Code development, maintenance and feature design.
items.feedbackers: All users who provided feedback and testing
items.feedbackers_desc: Filed issues and suggestions during real‑world usage and helped the project improve continuously.
items.cursor: Significantly improved development efficiency during refactors and iterations.

handler_option.arclight: Arclight / Mohist and similar hybrid servers

form.handler_desc: Different server types have very different outputs and commands. The server handler is the module that adapts MCDR to each server type and is the main entry point for controlling the server.

handler_detail.vanilla: For pure vanilla or simple single‑world servers. If you are not sure about your server type, this is usually the safest choice.
handler_detail.beta18: Compatibility handler for very old vanilla servers around Beta 1.8 and earlier, mainly for maintaining legacy worlds.
handler_detail.bukkit: For classic Bukkit‑family servers such as Bukkit / Spigot / Paper and most plugin‑centric servers.
handler_detail.bukkit14: Special compatibility for the historical Bukkit 1.4 branch. Only use this if you explicitly run that old version.
handler_detail.forge: For Forge‑based modded servers, where console output and commands follow the Forge conventions.
handler_detail.cat_server: Dedicated handler for CatServer, a hybrid implementation combining Forge and Bukkit features.
handler_detail.arclight: For Arclight, Mohist and similar hybrid servers that load both mods and Bukkit plugins.
handler_detail.bungeecord: For BungeeCord proxy servers that route traffic to multiple backend servers instead of running worlds directly.
handler_detail.waterfall: For Waterfall / Travertine and similar BungeeCord‑derived proxies. Use this when you run those proxy forks.
handler_detail.velocity: For Velocity proxy servers, a modern high‑performance proxy suitable for multi‑backend clusters.
handler_detail.basic: A generic console handler for servers that do not fit into the above categories or only need minimal command forwarding.

form.plugin_directories_tip: List of directories where MCDR looks for plugins. Usually you don't need to change this.
form.check_update_tip: Default: true. When enabled, MCDR will check for updates every 24 hours
